report.summary: Two separate root causes. The app's book list ignores the owner, so every user sees every user's books: this breaks the API isolation test and the new-user empty-bookshelf UI test (product bug, fix `list_books` in app/main.py first). The two add-book UI tests fail because the page object clicks `data-testid="add-books"` while the template renders `add-book` (test bug, one-line fix in tests/support/pages.py).

causes.title: GET /api/books and the /books page list every user's books
causes.explanation: list_books(user_id) takes the user id but never uses it. The query selects all rows from books, so any logged-in user gets books owned by other users. get_own_book, used for single-book GET, PUT and DELETE, does filter by owner_id, which is why those paths are correct and only the list endpoint and the bookshelf page leak. The API test fails on the list check. The UI test fails because a brand-new user's page shows other users' rows, so the empty-state element is never rendered.
evidence: tests\api\test_books_api.py:42: assert book["id"] not in other_ids  ->  AssertionError: assert 2 not in [1, 2]
app/main.py:147-150: def list_books(user_id: int) -> list[dict]: ... rows = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM books ORDER BY id").fetchall()  (user_id unused, no WHERE owner_id)
app/main.py:163-166: get_own_book filters with "WHERE id = ? AND owner_id = ?" (correct, so the 404 assertions in the same test are not the problem)
app/main.py:252-253: render_books passes books=list_books(user["id"]) to the template, so the /books page inherits the leak

Aria snapshot of the failing UI test shows a freshly registered user's table with rows "Final title Someone 2001" and "From API-7eba9a2e Robot", which belong to other users, and no empty-state paragraph: "Expect to_be_visible get_by_test_id('empty-state') ... element(s) not found"
causes.suggested_fix: Change the query in list_books to "SELECT * FROM books WHERE owner_id = ? ORDER BY id" and pass (user_id,). Then rerun the API isolation test and test_new_user_lands_on_empty_bookshelf. Consider adding a UI test that user B's page does not show user A's title.

causes.title: Page object uses the wrong test id for the Add book button
causes.explanation: BooksPage.add clicks get_by_test_id("add-books"), but the template's submit button is data-testid="add-book". The locator never matches, so Playwright times out after 5 s before the form is submitted. The app is fine: the aria snapshot shows the button labelled "Add book", and the title, author and year fields are present with their test ids.
evidence: Failure: "playwright._impl._errors.TimeoutError: Locator.click: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. Call log: - waiting for get_by_test_id("add-books")"
Aria snapshot in the login failure lists "button 'Add book'" on the same page, so the button renders but under a different test id
causes.suggested_fix: In tests/support/pages.py line 44, change "add-books" to "add-book". Consider a shared constant or a single source of truth for test ids so this cannot drift again. Also check whether anything else in the test suite refers to test ids that differ from the template.
